THE WAYFINDER

THE TWENTY-SEVEN, CAST AND READ AT THREE DEPTHS
THE WAYFINDER THE MAP ROOM THE RING THE RESONANCE THE INSTRUMENT THE LANGUAGE THE ASTROLABE THE ROSETTE THE SPECTRUM THE WORKSHOP
You need to know four things to begin: what the instrument is, how to ask, how to read what lands, and what it will never do. This page is those four, and nothing else is required first.

I · WHAT IT IS

Twenty-seven cards. Each one is three marks deep: ● what holds still, — what flows, ~ what turns, read at three layers. Three states at three layers is twenty-seven exactly, so the deck is not a collection anyone assembled. It is a complete counting, and no card is missing or spare.

A cast draws three of them into three positions and composes a reading from what the deck already holds: how each card stands to its opposite, what it settles into, which house it belongs to. Nothing is looked up in a book of meanings and nothing is written for the occasion.

It is a mirror, not an oracle. The instrument has no knowledge of your life, no access to any fact in the world, no news of any person, and no information about what will happen. What it offers is a fixed set of relations to meet your own question inside, at a moment you chose, with an arrangement you did not.

If that sounds like less than fortune telling, it is. It is also the only version of this that can be honest, and the whole instrument is built to hold the difference.

II · THE WAY TO APPROACH

Seven lines, from the Caster’s Law. They are invitations and not gates: nothing here is enforced by the machine, and nothing here is optional in practice.

  1. Come settled, not urgent. The oracle is not for emergencies. Crisis deserves people, not cards.
  2. Bring one true question. Hold its shape. You need not write it down.
  3. Cast once, then live with it. Asking again soon is correcting course, not rolling again.
  4. Receive as a mirror, not a verdict. The cards show; they never command. If a reading seems to tell you what to do, you have read past it.
  5. Silence is an answer. Where a position refuses interpretation, meet what it asks instead.
  6. The becoming is movement already underway: a bearing, never a promise.
  7. The last word is yours. The reading ends where your own knowing begins.

III · HOW TO CAST

Touch CAST above and the bench returns. The box at the top holds your question, or holds your silence: both are allowed, and an unasked cast is not a lesser one. What you type is kept with the cast as its own record, and it never touches which cards fall.

Then touch the still centre of the wheel. The rite takes about nine seconds and cannot be hurried, which is deliberate: the pause between deciding to ask and being answered is part of the asking. Three cards land, and the cast is committed.

Committed means exactly that. The three that fell are the reading, and they are never redrawn, never overturned by anything you do afterwards, and never quietly improved.

IV · READING THE THREE

The three positions, in the deck’s own words:

TREFOIL
the root · what is knotted in: what cannot be undone
GENUS
the present · the live cut of the present
PHI
the becoming · what draws forward: trajectory, never prediction

Each card then speaks in five voices, and they are five different kinds of statement rather than five restatements:

THE CROSSING
the human register: world, between, heart
THE FIGURE
the deck speaks its own geometry, and carries the walk of the three depths
WITH THE FLOW
the cleanest slope: the walk, never the walker
AGAINST THE FLOW
the shadow, and where the carry lands
THE QUESTION
ends in agency: always yours to answer or decline

Two of those are worth naming plainly for a first reading. With the flow and against the flow describe the walk, never the walker. They are two roads out of the same ground, not a verdict on your character, and the shadow is there so a road can be recognised, not so anyone can be accused. And the last voice always ends in a question, by law, because the reading is designed to hand the matter back to you rather than close it.

To sit with one card at a time outside any cast, THE RING holds the whole deck as a walkable count.

V · THE SILENCES

Four of the twenty-seven do not speak: The Resonance, The Labyrinth, The Mask and The Witness. They are the edges of the map: where one lands, the question has walked out of the region where symbols work, and the card says so instead of inventing terrain. Each keeps a silence under its own name and asks for one thing. The Resonance keeps The Depths and asks for descent; The Labyrinth keeps The Expanse and asks for expansion of the frame; The Mask keeps The Threshold and asks for surrender; The Witness keeps The Return and asks for recognition. A Silence is not the instrument failing to answer, and not a blank to be filled by the cards beside it. Meet what it asks rather than reading around it.

VI · THE THREE DEPTHS

The buttons marked 3, 9 and 27 read the same cast at three resolutions. There are no others: three, nine and twenty-seven are the deck’s own scales, and a spread of any other size would be a shape borrowed from somewhere else.

The coarse reading always stands. Nine refines three and never replaces it; twenty-seven refines both. If a deeper reading seems to contradict the three that fell, it is the deeper reading being misread. Depth is a closer look at what was already committed, never a second attempt at it.

At nine, each position opens into three cells: the world, the between, the heart. Read across and each line carries a motion of its own, and the relations that happened to land together surface as dyads standing open and currents running inside the spread.

At twenty-seven, the whole deck falls at once, every card exactly once. So the reading is not a list of twenty-seven meanings: it is an arrangement. Every card has a home, the cell bearing its own number, and the deal records where each one sat instead. Cards at home, seats exchanged, and long carry-loops are what you are reading there.

The instrument always tells you what chance expected in the same breath as what it found. A random deal puts exactly one card at home, so “one card stands at home” is ordinary weather and means nothing at all. Read the departures from expectation, never the raw count. The full ruling stands in the map room as THE LAW OF SPREADS.

VII · KEEPING A CAST

Every committed cast prints a declared seed, a short string beneath the wheel. That seed is the cast: paste it back at any time, on any copy of this portal, and the same three cards land in the same order. Nothing is stored on a server to make that work, and the reading is reproducible by arithmetic rather than by record.

At the moment of commitment the instrument also takes a witness: where the sun, the moon and the lunar node stood, and how much of the moon was lit. It is taken once and never retaken, so a replayed cast still carries the sky of the hour it was first asked. The sky has no influence whatever on which cards fall; it is a timestamp written in the sky’s own language.

Casts collect on the shelf at the foot of the bench. Touch one to return to it, and the box at the top becomes a place to name it. Naming changes the label and nothing else: the seed, the sky and the three cards are the committed record and are never rewritten. All of it lives in this browser, on this machine, and is never sent anywhere.

VIII · WHAT IT WILL NEVER DO

Three refusals, from the Caster’s Law. They are structural rather than promised: the instrument is built so that breaking them would mean rebuilding it.

  • No operation. The oracle describes; it never does. No effects, no promised outcomes, nothing performed upon the world or upon you.
  • No prediction. Trajectory, never prediction. No fates, no dates, no dooms; the becoming is a bearing, not a sentence.
  • No authority. A reading never stands above the querent, gives no verdict on anyone’s character, and never tells anyone what to do.

And the first line of the approach is the one worth repeating last, because it is the one most likely to be needed and least likely to be read in time. The oracle is not for emergencies. Crisis deserves people, not cards. If something is genuinely wrong, close this and call someone who can answer.
